title: What the City’s own documents say “other pay” is
question: What do the City’s published documents say the pay recorded outside salary and overtime consists of?
finding: The payroll file describes the column as irregular payments “including premium pay, incentive pay, or other one-time payments” and gives no breakdown. Other City documents on disk name the pieces without sizing them: premium pay and holiday pay in the police budget; retention pay and a signing bonus under the police agreement from July 2023; and unused leave, which the City’s accounts say “consist of vacation, sick, compensatory time, and other holidays and leaves”. No document on disk says how much of the yearly total is premiums, how much is leave paid out and how much is bonus or incentive pay, so the screens in this file do not say either.
how: The payroll file’s data dictionary, the City’s latest annual accounts, the pension fund’s latest valuation and the budget analyst’s reports in the project’s library were searched for the words premium, lump sum, cash out, vacation, sick leave, retention, incentive and bonus. Each row gives a one-sentence summary and a quotation of at most twelve words, checked word for word against the stored text, with the link recorded when the document was downloaded. For the valuation the date shown is the valuation date printed on its cover.
limits: These passages describe kinds of pay; none gives the amounts by kind, and the police agreement is one of many labour agreements. The labour agreements themselves, the Controller’s pay codes and the Retirement System’s board records on pay for its investment staff are not on disk. Nothing here should be read as saying that a particular payment in the tables above was of a particular kind.

rows.document: Employee Compensation dataset: description of the “Other Salaries” column
rows.said: The Controller’s own description of the column: irregular payments, of which it names three kinds. It gives no breakdown.
rows.quote: “including premium pay, incentive pay, or other one-time payments”

rows.document: 2025 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR), note on compensated absences
rows.said: The City’s accounts say the leave it owes staff, to be used or paid out on leaving, is made up of these kinds.
rows.quote: “consist of vacation, sick, compensatory time, and other holidays and leaves”

rows.document: 2025 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR), note on compensated absences
rows.said: A new accounting rule made the City recognize more of that unpaid leave in fiscal 2025, which lowered its opening net position by this amount.
rows.quote: “a $503.8 million decrease in the City’s beginning net position”

rows.document: Actuarial valuation report as of 1 July 2025, summary of plan provisions
rows.said: The pension fund’s plan summary says members pay contributions on salary without overtime and without most premium pay, which is why other pay mostly does not raise a pension.
rows.quote: “salary, excluding overtime and most premium pay”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Performance Audit of Police Dept Overtime
rows.said: The budget analyst reports the Controller’s estimate of $166.5 million for that agreement’s wage increases, retention pay, step adjustments and signing bonus together.
rows.quote: “wage increases, retention pay, step adjustments, and signing bonus”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: San Francisco Police Department FY 2022-23 Budget
rows.said: The budget analyst lists premium pay and holiday pay as parts of the police salary budget, separate from permanent salaries and overtime.
rows.quote: “includes permanent salaries, temporary salaries, premium pay, overtime, and holiday pay”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: San Francisco Police Department FY 2022-23 Budget
rows.said: The budget analyst describes the police agreement for fiscal 2024 to 2026 as adding retention pay after five, seven and eight years of service, and a one-time $600 bonus.
rows.quote: “three percent retention pay increases after five, seven, and eight years”
